seret.bin.note: Payload region is high-entropy and not decompressible with standard codecs (gzip/zlib/xz/lzma); consistent with an encrypted or non-standard-packed kernel payload.

secos.bin.note: Key most likely held in hardware (eFuse/OTP); not decryptable without an exploit. Not attempted.

ddr.init.note: Key most likely held in hardware (eFuse/OTP); not decryptable without an exploit. Not attempted.

sign.bin.interpretation: OpenSSL symmetric enc container (password/HW-key derived via EVP_BytesToKey). NOT a plaintext hash of the other components; without the hardware-held key it is neither reproducible nor forgeable.

arch_conclusion: EL3/secure monitor runs AArch32 (seret stub is a 32-bit zImage; stock kernel enters in AArch32 HYP). With a 32-bit EL3, SCR_EL3.RW cannot be set, so lower exception levels stay AArch32 and an AArch64 Linux cannot boot. The A57 cores are ARMv8 silicon, but this firmware permits only AArch32 -> target ARM 32-bit.
disclaimer: Descriptive, read-only inventory. No secure-boot validation, no bootability claim, no device flash. Research only.
